Subject: Discovery recap: Private VPC (Brightline Health) — next steps & requirements

Hi Samantha �14 thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please reply with any corrections or priorities we missed.

Summary of your goals / pain points
- Regulated PHI workloads across internal triage/chat features; must satisfy HIPAA and internal audit.
- Current stack: on-prem Kubernetes for core patient data + GCP for analytics; inference currently runs on a mix of GCP VMs and a managed API (high latency, cost concerns).
- Primary pain: need predictable latency and data isolation for inference that touches PHI; procurement wants minimal network egress and clear key custody.

Success criteria for Phase 1 (pilot)
- Private deployment (VPC peering or customer-managed VPC) with dedicated inference nodes, no logs leaving customer VPC except metrics agreed in SLA.
- Bring-your-own-keys (KMS/HSM) supported for model + request encryption at rest.
- Network constraints: allowlist of Redwood egress IPs OR VPN/Private Interconnect; support for air-gap or limited outbound connections if necessary.
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence + audit logs for model changes, access, and data egress.
- Pilot timeframe: 6–8 weeks from contract signature; demo to infra and security teams after initial network test.

Technical notes / requirements we captured
- Preferred deployment: Redwood Private in Brightline VPC with customer-provisioned subnets.
- KMS: Brightline will provision a Cloud HSM / KMS; Redwood must integrate with customer-managed keys (we can support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or an HSM-backed gateway).
- Data flow: inference requests remain within VPC; optional metrics/health telemetry can be forwarded to an agreed monitoring endpoint.
- Air-gap needs: if required, we can provide an offline bundle + on-prem package, but that will add ~3–4 weeks and require a signed L2 support engagement.

Open questions for your team
1) Desired network option: VPC peering, VPN, or dedicated interconnect? Which is procurement/security preference?
2) Do you have an existing KMS/HSM vendor we must integrate with (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Thales/HSM)?
3) Which log/telemetry retention window is acceptable for Brightline (30/90/365 days)?

Next steps
- Marissa: share private VPC checklist, high-level architecture, and SOC2 summary (attached).
- Brightline: confirm network option & primary infra contact for network test (name + email).
- Schedule 1-hr technical deep-dive with Rishi and Brightline infra/security (target week of Mar 2).

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf (network checklist & preflight), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

Thanks �14 looking forward to moving this forward.


Best,

Samantha / team �14 quick technical follow up from my side:

1) Network options
- VPN: fastest to set up for pilot; requires static egress allowlist and VPN tunnel configuration. We'll supply a minimal list of outbound endpoints for telemetry/OS packages.
- Interconnect: recommended for production if you need high throughput and lower latency; longer lead time and procurement work.

2) KMS/HSM integration
- We support Google Cloud KMS CMEK for encryption of model artifacts. For HSM-backed key wrap, we can support an HSM gateway that integrates with our runtime; we'll need access patterns and policies (key usage, rotation windows).

3) Air-gap / on-prem option
- If full air-gap is required, we can provide an offline deployment bundle and on-site installation steps. Note: offline bundle prevents automatic patching; we'll provide a signed support addendum and SOC2 scope implications.

4) Pilot sizing and pricing inputs we need
- Expected peak qps (inference requests/sec) and average sequence length (tokens) to recommend instance types and node counts.
- Required P95 latency SLO.

Attached: redwood-private-vpc-highlevel.pdf (high-level arch + network ports), brightline-network-requirements.xlsx (example firewall settings).

Happy to run through the deep-dive agenda on Tue Mar 2 at 10am PST �14 confirmed.
